gold_answer: Under Section 3(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025, tax year means the twelve months period of the financial year commencing on the 1st April.
An assessee is defined under Section 2(11) as a person by whom any tax or any other sum of money is payable under this Act.
Under Section 2(5), an approved gratuity fund is a gratuity fund approved and maintained under the Income-tax Act.
It refers to a public company satisfying public ownership and voting power thresholds under Section 2(18).
Population is defined under Section 3(4) as ascertained at the last preceding published census.
Under Section 2(38), property includes all kinds of property held by an assessee whether connected with business or not.
Securities are defined under Section 3(7) to include shares, stocks, debentures, and marketable securities.
Standard deduction from salary under Section 202(1) is fixed at Rs. 75,000.
Under Section 2(42), rates in force refer to the income tax rates specified in the relevant Finance Act.
Gross total income is the total income computed across all heads prior to Chapter VIA deductions.
Agricultural income under Section 2(1) includes rent, revenue, or income from land situated in India used for agricultural purposes.
Amalgamation is defined under Section 2(2) as the merger of companies where all property and liabilities transfer to the amalgamated company.
Under Section 2(3), annual value represents the reasonable expected annual rent of a house property.
Superannuation fund approved by the tax authority under Section 2(6).
Assessment under Section 2(8) includes regular assessment, reassessment, and best judgment assessment.
Under Section 2(12), it is the total tax payable divided by the total income.
Defined under Section 2(14) as a group of assets eligible for identical depreciation rates.
Under Section 2(15), business encompasses trade, commerce, manufacture, or concern in the nature of trade.
Capital asset is defined under Section 2(16) as property held by an assessee excluding stock-in-trade and personal effects.
Charitable purpose under Section 2(17) covers poor relief, education, yoga, healthcare, environment preservation, and public utility objects.
Dividend under Section 2(22) includes statutory distributions of accumulated profits to shareholders.
Income under Section 2(24) is an inclusive statutory term encompassing revenue gains, capital gains, perquisites, and trust contributions.
Defined under Section 2(26A) as a company financing or investing in infrastructure projects.
A capital asset held beyond statutory specified threshold (12/24/36 months) under Section 2(29A).
Defined under Section 2(29C) as the highest marginal tax rate plus applicable surcharge.
Person is defined under Section 2(31) to include individuals, HUFs, companies, firms, AOPs, BOIs, local authorities, and artificial juridical persons.
Defined under Section 2(35) as key administrative officers responsible for tax compliance.
Relative under Section 2(41) means spouse, siblings, and direct lineal ancestors or descendants.
Defined under Section 2(42A) based on holding period immediately prior to transfer.
Under Section 43(5), a contract settled without actual delivery of commodity or shares.
Transfer under Section 2(47) encompasses sale, exchange, relinquishment, compulsory acquisition, and extinguishment of rights.
Defined under Section 2(48) as a discounted bond with no intermediate interest payments.
Under Section 35AD(8), specified capital-intensive infrastructure and industrial businesses.
Defined under Section 2(42C) as undertaking transfer for a consolidated lump-sum price.
A partnership firm satisfying statutory registration conditions under Section 2(39).
Defined under Section 2(14) based on municipal status and minimum population threshold.
Under Section 2(33), prescribed means set down under the official Income-tax Rules by CBDT.
Defined under Section 2(38A) as a provident fund approved under tax rules.
The threshold specified in Part I of the First Schedule to Finance Act 2026.
Non-resident entities without permanent establishment as clarified in CBDT Circular 1/2026.
An employee is eligible on retirement, superannuation, or resignation after continuous service under Section 6.
Pension commutation is eligible under Section 7 when received under statutory pension rules.
Individual taxpayers receiving salary income are eligible for standard deduction under Section 202.
Assessees donating to Lieutenant Governor's Relief Fund are eligible for 100% deduction under Section 133.
Donations to Swachh Bharat Kosh qualify for 100% deduction provided they are non-CSR contributions under Section 133.
Resident assessees are eligible for 100% deduction for contributions to Clean Ganga Fund under Section 133.
Employees are eligible for deduction under Section 124(1) up to 14% (Central Govt) or 10% (others) of salary.
HUFs making donations to approved trusts are eligible for deduction under Section 123.
Government employees receive full leave encashment exemption under Section 10(10AA).
Workmen are eligible for retrenchment exemption under Section 10(10B) up to Rs. 5 lakhs.
Employees taking VRS under approved guidelines qualify for exemption up to Rs. 5 lakhs under Section 10(10C).
Salaried taxpayers occupying rented residential premises qualify for HRA exemption under Section 10(13A).
Individual and HUF assessees paying health insurance premiums qualify under Section 80D.
Resident individuals and HUFs maintaining disabled dependents qualify under Section 80DD.
Individual taxpayers paying higher education loan interest qualify for 8-year deduction under Section 80E.
Individuals purchasing electric vehicles on institutional loans qualify under Section 80EEB.
Non-business assessees making donations to approved research institutions qualify under Section 80GGA.
Persons making non-cash donations to registered political parties qualify under Section 80GGC.
Corporate and audited assessees creating new employment qualify for 30% deduction under Section 80JJAA.
Resident individual patent inventors qualify for royalty deduction under Section 80RRB.
Individual and HUF non-senior citizen taxpayers qualify under Section 80TTA.
Resident senior citizens earning interest on bank or post office deposits qualify under Section 80TTB.
Small resident businesses with turnover below threshold qualify under Section 44AD.
Specified resident professionals with receipts below threshold qualify under Section 44ADA.
Transporters owning no more than 10 goods vehicles qualify under Section 44AE.
Recognized eligible startups satisfying turnover and incorporation criteria qualify under Section 80IAC.
Tea, coffee, and rubber growers depositing funds with NABARD qualify under Section 33AB.
Petroleum and gas extraction entities depositing funds in SBI account qualify under Section 33ABA.
Telecom license holders paying capital fees qualify for amortization under Section 35ABB.
Assessees funding notified agricultural training and extension projects qualify under Section 35CCC.
Manufacturing companies spending on notified skill training qualify under Section 35CCD.
Indian companies and resident assessees incurring setup expenses qualify under Section 35D.
Indian companies undergoing corporate restructuring qualify under Section 35DD.
Employers paying VRS compensation qualify for 5-year amortization under Section 35DDA.
Employers paying employee bonus or commission qualify under Section 36(1)(ii).
Business assessees writing off irrecoverable trade debts qualify under Section 36(1)(vii).
Corporate employers promoting family planning qualify for 5-year capital deduction under Section 36(1)(ix).
Share traders declaring business income qualify for STT deduction under Section 36(1)(xv).
Taxpayers calculating fair market value of indirect Indian asset transfers qualify under Rule 11CB.
Software distributors satisfying Circular 3/2026 conditions qualify for non-withholding.
The maximum standard deduction allowed from salary is Rs. 75,000 under Section 202.
The TDS threshold for professional fees under Section 194J is Rs. 30,000 per financial year.
TDS threshold under Section 194C is Rs. 30,000 for single credit or Rs. 1,00,000 aggregate.
TDS rate under Section 194A is 10% above Rs. 40,000 threshold (Rs. 50,000 for senior citizens).
Rent TDS threshold under Section 194I is Rs. 2,40,000 per financial year.
Property purchase TDS threshold under Section 194IA is Rs. 50,00,000 at 1% rate.
Monthly rent threshold for individual TDS under Section 194IB is Rs. 50,000 per month.
Goods purchase TDS threshold under Section 194Q is Rs. 50 lakhs at 0.1% rate.
TCS threshold on goods sale under Section 206C(1H) is Rs. 50 lakhs at 0.1%.
LRS remittance TCS rate is 20% above Rs. 7 lakh threshold under Section 206C(1G).
Higher penal TDS rate for non-PAN deductees is 20% under Section 206AA.
TDS for non-filers under Section 206AB is twice the applicable rate or 5%.
Senior citizen basic tax exemption is Rs. 3,00,000 under Finance Act 2026.
Super senior citizen basic tax exemption threshold is Rs. 5,00,000 under Finance Act 2026.
Section 87A rebate for new tax regime applies up to Rs. 7 lakh income (Rs. 25,000 rebate).
Individual income surcharge starts at 10% above Rs. 50 lakh income threshold.
Surcharge under new tax regime is capped at 25% under Finance Act 2026.
Health and Education Cess rate is fixed at 4% across all income slabs.
Tax rate for new manufacturing companies under Section 115BAB is 15% plus surcharge and cess.
Domestic company concessional tax rate under Section 115BAA is 22% (effective ~25.17%).
MAT rate on corporate book profit under Section 115JB is 15%.
AMT rate under Section 115JC is 18.5% of adjusted total income.
Short-term capital gains tax rate under Section 111A is 20%.
LTCG tax rate under Section 112A is 12.5% above Rs. 1.25 lakh annual exemption.
Virtual Digital Assets tax rate under Section 115BBH is 30% without expense deduction.
VDA TDS rate under Section 194S is 1% above Rs. 50,000 annual threshold.
Cash withdrawal TDS threshold under Section 194N is Rs. 1 crore (Rs. 20 lakh for non-filers).
Business benefit TDS threshold under Section 194R is Rs. 20,000 at 10% rate.
Online gaming winnings tax rate under Section 115BBJ is 30%.
TDS on online gaming under Section 194BA is 30% on net winnings without minimum threshold.
Employer accommodation perquisite under Rule 3 is valued at 10%, 7.5%, or 5% of salary.
Fair market value of unquoted shares under Rule 11UA is calculated using book value formula.
Transport allowance exemption for disabled employees under Rule 2BB is Rs. 3,200 per month.
Education allowance exemption under Rule 2BB is Rs. 100 per month per child (max 2 children).
Hostel allowance exemption under Rule 2BB is Rs. 300 per month per child (max 2 children).
Interest waiver threshold under CBDT Circular 4/2026 is Rs. 500,000.
Departmental appeal filing monetary thresholds under Circular 6/2026 are Rs. 50L (ITAT), Rs. 1Cr (HC), Rs. 2Cr (SC).
LTCG tax rate under Section 112A was amended to 12.5% by Finance Act 2025.
STCG tax rate under Section 111A was increased to 20% by Finance Act 2024 (No. 2).
New tax regime basic exemption was raised to Rs. 3 lakh by Finance Act 2023.
CSR expenditure is explicitly disallowed as a business expense under Explanation 2 to Section 37(1).
Cash payments exceeding Rs. 10,000 in a day are 100% disallowed under Section 40A(3).
30% of payment to resident is disallowed upon TDS default under Section 40(a)(ia).
100% of payment to non-resident is disallowed upon TDS default under Section 40(a)(i).
MSME supplier payments paid beyond statutory credit period are disallowed under Section 43B(h) until actual payment.
Rural agricultural land in India is excluded from capital asset definition under Section 2(14).
Personal effects (excluding jewellery and artwork) are excluded from capital assets under Section 2(14).
Inter-corporate dividends distributed before tax filing due date are exempt from double tax under Section 80M.
Transfers via gift, will, or irrevocable trust are excluded from capital gains under Section 47(iii).
Asset transfer in amalgamation to an Indian company is exempt from capital gains under Section 47(vi).
Asset transfer in demerger to a resulting Indian company is exempt under Section 47(vib).
Minor child income is not clubbed with parent's income if minor has Section 80U disability under Section 64(1A).
Income earned by minor through personal talent, skill, or manual work is excluded from clubbing under Section 64(1A).
Gifts received by an individual on the occasion of marriage are exempt from gift tax under Section 56(2)(x).
Property received under a will or inheritance is completely exempt from tax under Section 56(2)(x).
Money or property received from defined relatives is 100% tax-free under Section 56(2)(x).
Speculative business loss can only be set off against speculative business profits under Section 73.
Long-term capital loss cannot be set off against short-term capital gains under Section 70(3).
Government, banks, and post office savings banks are exempt from Section 269SS cash loan bar.
Cash repayment to Government or banks is exempt from Section 269T penalty.
Non-compete fees received for refraining from business are taxable under Section 28(va).
Small taxpayers declaring profit at 8%/6% under Section 44AD are exempt from Section 44AB tax audit.
Self-occupied house property loan interest deduction is capped at Rs. 2 lakhs under Section 24(b).
Compulsory government acquisition of urban agricultural land is 100% exempt under Section 10(37).
Medical treatment expenses abroad are exempt perquisite up to RBI ceiling under Rule 3D.
Pro-rata bonus share allotment is exempt from fair market valuation under Rule 11AAE.
Non-resident shipping freights covered under Section 172 are exempt from TDS as per Circular 2/2026.
Technical software TDS short-deduction defaults are exempt from penalty per Circular 5/2026.
STT is strictly non-deductible against capital gains under Finance Act 2026.
Investments in DPIIT recognized startups are exempt from angel tax under Finance Act 2025.
Technical service payments are subject to 2% TDS under Section 194J, overriding general contract TDS under Section 194C.
TDS is deducted at the highest resulting rate between Section 206AA (20%) and Section 206AB.
Section 194Q buyer TDS takes priority over Section 206C(1H) seller TCS on goods purchase.
Taxpayers declaring presumptive profit below 8%/6% with income above exemption must undergo Section 44AB audit.
Section 50C governs capital gains on land/building while Section 43CA governs business profits on real estate inventory.
Intra-head setoff under Section 70 is mandatory prior to seeking inter-head setoff under Section 71.
Business perquisites are taxed under Section 28(iv) whereas personal unrequited gifts are taxed under Section 56(2)(x).
Section 80GG rent deduction is mutually exclusive with Section 10(13A) HRA exemption.
Section 115BAC restricts Chapter VIA deductions to employer pension and new employment cost.
Section 194M covers individual personal payments over Rs. 50 lakh not subject to 194C/194J.
International arm's length pricing is governed by Section 92C while domestic excessive related payments are controlled by Section 40A(2).
Failure to adhere to Section 269SS cash threshold results in 100% penalty under Section 271D.
Repaying deposits in cash over Rs. 20,000 triggers 100% penalty under Section 271E.
Excess MAT paid under Section 115JB creates a 15-year carry-forward MAT credit under Section 115JAA.
Section 14A disallows expenses relating to exempt income using the formula specified in Rule 8D.
Section 45 creates capital gains liability while Section 48 prescribes full value of consideration less acquisition costs.
Section 54 requires transfer of residential house; Section 54F requires transfer of non-residential asset reinvested in a house.
Sections 234A, 234B, and 234C penalize delay in filing, shortfall in advance tax, and deferment of quarterly advance tax respectively.
Section 139(1) specifies original statutory due date while Section 139(4) permits belated filing with penalty.
Both original (139(1)) and belated (139(4)) returns can be revised under Section 139(5).
Section 194J requires professional TDS deduction, which must be quarterly reported in Form 26Q per Rule 31A.
Section 112A LTCG rate of 12.5% is enacted via Finance Act 2025 amendment.
Circular 2/2026 provides administrative relaxation exempting non-resident shipping freight from Section 194C TDS.
Section 14A provides statutory disallowance while Rule 8D provides the mathematical computation formula.
Section 44AB mandates tax audit, and Rule 6G prescribes filing audit reports in Forms 3CA/3CB and 3CD.
Section 92C sets statutory arm's length mandate, and Rule 10B details specific calculation methods.
Section 10(13A) creates statutory HRA exemption, and Rule 2A defines exact limits.
Section 80DDB grants medical deduction while Rule 11DD enumerates qualifying medical conditions.
Section 206C imposes LRS TCS, and Circular 1/2026 provides procedural administrative guidelines.
Section 115BAC provides option framework while Finance Act 2026 enacts exact annual slab rates.
Section 194IA mandates property TDS, and Rule 31A prescribes Form 26QB filing.
Section 194IB creates individual rent TDS liability, and Rule 31A prescribes Form 26QC.
Section 194M mandates personal payment TDS, and Rule 31A prescribes Form 26QD.
Section 194S creates crypto TDS obligation, and Rule 31A prescribes Form 26QE reporting.
Section 269SU mandates electronic payment facility, and Rule 11DD specifies UPI and RuPay modes.
Section 115BBH imposes 30% VDA tax, and Circular 4/2026 clarifies strict loss setoff prohibition.
Section 139A mandates PAN requirement, and Rule 114 sets down Form 49A application procedures.
Section 139AA requires Aadhaar linking, and Rule 114AAA prescribes Rs. 1,000 delay fee.
Section 285BA mandates Statement of Financial Transactions, and Rule 114E specifies reporting limits.
Section 90 grants statutory DTAA relief, and Rule 128 mandates Form 67 filing for Foreign Tax Credit.
Finance Act 2022 enacted 30% tax on virtual digital assets starting Assessment Year 2023-24.
New tax regime under Section 115BAC became default from Assessment Year 2024-25 via Finance Act 2023.
LTCG tax rate under Section 112A was increased to 12.5% effective 23rd July 2024 by Finance Act 2024 (No. 2).
STCG tax rate under Section 111A was increased to 20% effective 23rd July 2024 by Finance Act 2024 (No. 2).
Rebate under Section 87A remains available up to Rs. 7 lakh income under new tax regime in Finance Act 2025.
Basic exemption limits and tax rates for Assessment Year 2027-28 are enacted under Finance Act 2026.
Section 54 and 54F capital gains exemptions were capped at Rs. 10 crore starting AY 2024-25 by Finance Act 2023.
Updated return provision under Section 139(8A) was introduced by Finance Act 2022 allowing 2-year filing window.
Indexation benefit for real estate LTCG was removed for transfers post 23rd July 2024 by Finance Act 2024 (No. 2).
Angel tax under Section 56(2)(viib) was extended to non-resident investors by Finance Act 2023.
Section 194R business benefit TDS was introduced by Finance Act 2022 effective 1st July 2022.
Section 194S VDA TDS was introduced by Finance Act 2022 effective 1st July 2022.
Online gaming TDS under Section 194BA was enacted by Finance Act 2023 effective 1st April 2023.
STT rates on F&O trades were increased by Finance Act 2024 (No. 2) effective 1st October 2024.
Startup incorporation date for Section 80IAC tax holiday was extended to 1st April 2026 by Finance Act 2025.
The tax audit report under Section 44AB must be filed by 30th September of the assessment year.
TDS quarterly return due dates under Rule 31A are 31st July, 31st October, 31st January, and 31st May.
Form 16 salary TDS certificate must be issued by 15th June per Rule 31.
Form 16A must be issued within 15 days of quarterly TDS return filing deadline under Rule 31.
PAN application is filed in Form 49A per procedure under Rule 114.
Unlinked PAN becomes inoperative leading to higher TDS and withheld refunds under Rule 114AAA.
Form 10E must be electronically submitted prior to tax return filing to claim Section 89 relief under Rule 21AA.
Form 67 must be filed on or before tax return due date to claim Foreign Tax Credit under Rule 128.
Advance tax payment due dates under Section 211 are 15th June (15%), 15th Sep (45%), 15th Dec (75%), 15th Mar (100%).
Section 139(8A) allows 24-month filing with 25%/50% additional tax under Section 140B.
Form 61A SFT annual statement must be filed by 31st May per Rule 114E.
Nil TDS self-declarations Form 15G/15H must be processed per Rule 29C.
Charitable trust registration application is submitted in Form 10A per Rule 17A.
Charitable trust audit report must be filed in Form 10B/10BB per Rule 17B.
Foreign Portfolio Investor compliance deadline is extended to 30th June 2026 under CBDT Circular 1/2026.
